q1_issues.issue: The quoted proposition is negative ("I don't even worry about that") but the sealed complement is the bare positive worry bundle, so the parse records the speaker as saying he does worry — the instruction set explicitly says a seal that cannot carry polarity is not a licence to assert the positive form.
(Past sk_worry_1) contradicts the quote's present tense ("I don't worry"), which is unmarked, not past.
"anymore" is dropped — the cessation reading (the worrying held and no longer holds) leaves no trace at all.
"that" is a demonstrative, hence definite, so its (Member sk_thing_1 thing) typing should project outside the seal rather than sit inside it.
(Even worry sk_worry_1) sits at top level but anchors on sk_worry_1, an event symbol that exists only inside the sealed Theme term.

q2_gaps: direct quotation as a speech-verb complement ("...," X said) — the attitude section covers finite that-clauses only, and quote-internal first person ("I" = the speaker) has no coreference rule
a wholly negative sealed complement — the registered no-polarity-carrier limitation covers a negated conjunct among several, not a complement that is entirely negated
cessation ("not ... anymore") inside a seal: the same-symbol Past-plus-strength-0-denial pair cannot be expressed inside a sealed term
a psych verb with a prepositional object ("worry about that") — Stimulus vs the preposition-named oblique is undetermined, since the prepositional-verb rule names only Patient/Theme
notes: The matrix NP is handled well: center_fielder fused with its genus and no exposed noun modifier, plus the 38-year-old measure on the old scale. The defect is confined to the quoted proposition, whose polarity, tense and cessation are all lost.
